concepts.title: Classification and Nomenclature of Hydrocarbons
concepts.definition: Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen and are classified into saturated alkanes with sigma bonds only, unsaturated alkenes and alkynes with pi bonds, and aromatic hydrocarbons with benzene ring systems, each named by IUPAC rules with locants for multiple bonds and substituents.
concepts.key_idea: Alkanes follow the general formula CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n and alkynes CnH2n-2, showing the decreasing hydrogen content with unsaturation.

solution_steps.explain: Note single, double or triple bonds to pick the series.
Separate open chain from aromatic ring systems.
Use locants and longest chain for the IUPAC name.

concepts.title: Preparation and Properties of Alkanes, Alkenes and Alkynes
concepts.definition: Alkanes come from hydrogenation of alkenes, Wurtz reaction and decarboxylation; alkenes form by beta elimination of alkyl halides and dehydration of alcohols following Saytzeff rule; alkynes arise by dehydrohalogenation of vicinal dihalides, and all show combustion, addition and substitution reactions.
concepts.key_idea: Markovnikov's rule predicts the addition of unsymmetrical reagents to alkenes, while peroxide effect reverses the orientation for hydrogen bromide addition.

solution_steps.explain: Identify the precursor and reagent for the preparation.
Apply Markovnikov, Saytzeff or elimination logic to the product.
Confirm the product belongs to the right hydrocarbon series.

concepts.title: Aromatic Hydrocarbons: Benzene Structure, Aromaticity and Electrophilic Substitution
concepts.definition: Benzene, with a planar ring of six sp2 carbons and six delocalised pi electrons obeying Huckel's 4n plus 2 rule, shows aromaticity, resists addition and undergoes electrophilic substitution reactions of nitration, halogenation, sulphonation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation, with substituent directing effects deciding the orientation of the entering group.
concepts.key_idea: Ortho and para directors like the hydroxyl group activate the ring, while meta directors like the nitro group deactivate it, governing electrophilic substitution orientation.

solution_steps.explain: Check planarity, conjugation and the Huckel electron count.

concepts.title: Carcinogenicity and Uses of Hydrocarbons
concepts.definition: Polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons formed by incomplete combustion of fuels and tobacco are carcinogenic, entering the body and damaging DNA to cause cancer, while benzene and other hydrocarbons serve as fuels, solvents and starting materials for dyes, drugs and polymers.
concepts.key_idea: Health hazards of aromatic hydrocarbons link combustion chemistry to environmental and occupational safety.
